Edit the supplied image as a tightly localized structural study. Change only one joint in the nearest thick square terrace rim: the diagonal stone rim running from the screen-left corner downward toward the central white fissure, above and to the left of the standing figure. Place the edit around 30% of the image width and 45% of its height. Work only on this foreground terrace edge, not the terrace behind it.
The single visual goal is: one massive end visibly catches and supports the other, while the break remains open.
At this location, interrupt the existing rim with one irregular fracture. Keep the screen-left outer section in its existing position. Give its lower portion a short, thick, integral stone lip extending toward screen-right beneath the other section. The screen-right section, which continues toward the central fissure, has slipped slightly downward. Its broken underside rests directly on that lower lip at one clearly visible bearing point.
Make the overlap legible through occlusion. The right-hand block sits above the supporting lip and hides part of the lip's upper surface. A narrow exposed shelf of the left-hand lip remains visible immediately beside the contact. The left-hand supporting mass continues visibly underneath the right-hand block. There must be no air gap at the bearing point.
Above this support, leave a clearly open, dark, irregular slit between the two broken upper faces. The slit cuts across the terrace's top surface and remains visible down its front face until it reaches the small underside bearing contact. The upper faces do not reconnect. The result should read as a heavy broken end being caught, with its wound still open, rather than two unrelated broken bridges or a repaired seamless joint.
Use the existing dark stone, thickness, perspective, and restrained cold edge lighting. Make the local silhouettes and broad planes sufficiently clear to read the support without labels. Add no bracket, pillar, cable, keystone, extra platform, glowing connection, or hand-shaped rock.
Preserve everything outside this small joint, including both people and their exact pose, the walkway and railings, the central mountain and vertical axis, all other terrace edges, the red patch, every star group, the outer star field, the camera, and the overall scale and contrast. Do not connect the structure to the people with light or energy. Do not add symbols or text.
